enzyme-rate-factors.alt: Three sketch graphs of reaction rate. Against temperature, the rate rises to a peak near 37 degrees Celsius for a human enzyme and then falls steeply as the enzyme denatures. Against pH, pepsin peaks near pH 2 and trypsin near pH 8. Against substrate concentration, the rate rises and levels off; a competitive inhibitor slows the rise but approaches the same maximum, while a noncompetitive inhibitor levels off at a lower maximum.

enzyme-inhibition.alt: Two enzymes side by side. On the left, a competitive inhibitor shaped like the substrate sits in the active site and the substrate is blocked. On the right, a noncompetitive inhibitor binds a separate allosteric site at the bottom of the enzyme, the active site at the top is bent out of shape, and the substrate no longer fits.
